meta.title: Published Invoke — the production request lifecycle
meta.subtitle: POST /v1/agents/:id/invoke: token auth → tenant pin (RLS) → spend + Vault key → runtime.invoke → Run record

messages.label: decrypt provider key (JIT)

cards.title: Caller-token auth
items: Strip 'Bearer ', sha256 the secret → lookup api_tokens.token_hash (only the hash is ever stored)
Reject on revoked_at or expires_at; per-token rate-limit via a Redis sliding window
CallerCtx carries {workspace_id, token_id, role=executer, teams, scopes} — the FE runtime-access decode, now server-authoritative

cards.title: Admit & isolate
items: SET LOCAL app.workspace_id pins the tenant for the request — PgBouncer MUST be transaction-pool mode or it leaks across callers
BudgetGuard reserves spend up-front, reconciles against actual after the run (402 if over cap)
[P2] concurrency slot; idempotency_key dedupe so a retried call can't double-run or double-bill

cards.title: Effective access (fail-closed)
items: canUse runs BEFORE any provider call: access = agent config ∩ caller grants ∩ tenant ∩ resource policy
A token/channel caller carries no owner subject → private resources deny for every caller (admin is a console claim, not a token)
Denied tools / KBs / skills are dropped from the run, not errored

cards.title: Same core, fully recorded
items: runtime.invoke(run_source=api) is the SAME code playground + eval run — the drift guarantee holds in prod
Provider key is Vault-decrypted just-in-time into memory and discarded after the call
The Run is tagged caller_token_id + workspace_id so cost attributes to the endpoint; events re-encode 1:1 to SSE
